title: Dinho Ouro Preto Reveals Renato Russo Tribute Show at Rock in Rio
seoTitle: Dinho Ouro Preto Announces Renato Russo Tribute at Rock.
subtitle: Capital Inicial Prepares Special Performance with Dado Villa-Lobos to Celebrate 30 Years Since the Death of the Brazilian Rock Icon
excerpt: Dinho Ouro Preto announced that Capital Inicial will perform a special show at Rock in Rio, honoring Renato Russo on the 30th anniversary of his passing, with the.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Dinho Ouro Preto, frontman of Capital Inicial, revealed that the band will present a special show at the upcoming Rock in Rio, dedicated to the memory of Renato Russo. The news was announced during the Almas Novas event, held in Lavras Novas, a district of Ouro Preto, Minas Gerais.

Dinho Ouro Preto Announces Rock in Rio Show

The announcement was made on Saturday (29) and is already circulating among national rock fans, who are awaiting the festival's lineup. Dinho used the occasion to confirm that the repertoire will be focused on Renato Russo's work.

Tribute to Renato Russo Marks 30th Anniversary of His Death

The performance coincides with the commemoration of three decades since Renato Russo's death, which occurred on October 11, 1996, at the age of 36. The date reinforces the importance of the singer and songwriter's legacy for successive generations.

Dado Villa-Lobos' Participation Reinforces Historical Ties

Dado Villa-Lobos, guitarist for Legião Urbana, has been confirmed as a special guest. His presence symbolizes the connection between the two bands, which share origins in the group Aborto Elétrico, where Dinho and Renato Russo played together.

Repertoire Promises to Revive Legião Urbana Classics

The show is expected to revisit songs associated with Renato Russo's and Legião Urbana's trajectory, such as "Tempo Perdido," "Pais e Filhos," and "Eduardo e Mônica." The goal is to create a tribute that unites memory and musical influence.

Fan Expectation and Cultural Significance

Fans of Capital Inicial, Legião Urbana, and Renato Russo show great anticipation, emphasizing the importance of celebrating a body of work that continues to resonate in lyrics sung by different generations. The event reinforces Brazilian rock's role as a voice for youth, politics, and collective emotions.

With information from Jornal Geraes.
